item.title: EGMR (Schweiz) 20261105_38204_19 vom 2026-11-05
item.description:
Urteilskopf 38204/19 Alonso Radesca et autres c. Suisse Arrêt no. 38204/19, 05 novembre 2026
Regeste Diese Zusammenfassung existiert nur auf Französisch. SUISSE: Art. 11 CEDH. Licenciement d'employés d'un hôpital privé au motif qu'ils avaient participé à une grève jugée illégale par les juridictions internes; condamnations pénales pour violation de propriété privée, à raison de l'organisation d'un piquet de grève sur les lieux de l'hôpital, de secrétaires des syndicats chargés de conduire les négociations. La grève avait eu lieu à la suite du retrait de l'hôpital d'une convention collective. Les autorités nationales avaient jugé la grève illicite, ce qui avait entraîné le licenciement des employés de l'hôpital qui y avaient participé et l'imposition de sanctions pénales aux secrétaires syndicaux qui avaient été mandatés pour mener les négociations. Selon la Cour, ni l'art. 28 Cst., qui garantit le droit de grève, ni la jurisprudence nationale, ne fournissaient une base claire permettant de comprendre qu'une grève licite pouvait devenir illicite à partir du moment où un tribunal, avec le bénéfice du recul, avait considéré qu'un employeur avait proposé des conditions qui rendaient inutile la poursuite de la grève. Une telle interprétation a fait naître une importante incertitude pour les syndicats et les salariés quant aux circonstances dans lesquelles ils pouvaient poursuivre l'action collective en conservant la protection offerte par le droit national (ch. 117-146 et ch. 147-159). Conclusion: violation de l'art. 11 CEDH. Sachverhalt FIFTH SECTION CASE OF ALONSO RADESCA AND OTHERS v. SWITZERLAND (Applications nos. 38204/19 and 2 others - see appended list) JUDGMENT Art 11 - Positive obligations - Freedom of assembly and association - Dismissal of private hospital employees for participating in a strike deemed unlawful by the domestic courts - Domestic courts' failure to comply with their positive obligations by failing to secure applicants' right to strike - Interpretation of domestic law created a significant degree of uncertainty for unions and employees as to the circumstances in which they continued collective action while retaining the protection afforded by domestic law - Interpretation not sufficiently foreseeable in its application in the applicants' situation - Essence of the right to strike undermined - Lack of balancing exercise between competing private interests Art 11 - Freedom of assembly and association - Criminal convictions for trespassing, as a result of organising a picket line on the hospital grounds, of secretaries of the trade unions mandated to conduct the strike negotiations in the context of their trade union activity - Convictions for non-violent actions, fully within the trade unionists' mandate and did not cause damage - Fines imposed with chilling effect on trade union members and an impact on the applicants' professional lives as trade union representatives - Disproportionate interference not compatible with a "pressing social need" and thus not "necessary in a democratic society" Prepared by the Registry. Does not bind the Court. STRASBOURG 5 November 2026 This judgment will become final in the circumstances set out in Article 44 § 2 of the Convention. It may be subject to editorial revision. In the case of Alonso Radesca and Others v. Switzerland, The European Court of Human Rights (Fifth Section), sitting as a Chamber composed of: Kateřina Šimáčková , President , Gilberto Felici, Andreas Zünd, Mykola Gnatovskyy, Vahe Grigoryan, Sébastien Biancheri, Nicholas Emiliou , judges , and Martina Keller, Deputy Section Registrar, Having regard to: the applications (nos. 38204/19, 30379/21 and 30786/21) against the Swiss Confederation lodged with the Court under Article 34 of the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms ("the Convention") by twenty Swiss nationals and one French national ("the applicants"), on the various dates indicated in the appended table; the decision to give notice of the applications to the Swiss Government ("the Government"); the observations submitted by the respondent Government and the observations in reply submitted by the applicants; the letter from the French Government informing the Court that they do not wish to make use of their right to intervene in the proceedings in respect of application no. 38204/19 (Article 36 § 1 of the Convention); the comments submitted by the European Trade Union Confederation, who were granted leave by the President of the Section to intervene in the written procedure; Having deliberated in private on 29 September 2026, Delivers the following judgment, which was adopted on that date: INTRODUCTION 1. The case concerns a strike in a private hospital over its withdrawal from a collective bargaining agreement.
